structure.summary: Multi-turn, one question per message. Questions go through the picker where one exists; eval runs have none, so they use the plain-markdown fallback. Each later message opens with a one-line ✓ echo of the last answer, then the next question. After the last answer comes a bulleted list of echoes and a one-sentence confirmation request; after confirmation, a short paragraph on what will be done, then the work.

elements.description: Fallback question: a bold heading line `**Question N of T · Label**`, the question on the next line, 2-4 options as a bulleted list of `**X · label**: sentence`, then one reply-hint line starting with `Reply`. No code block, box drawing or emoji.
Each option's sentence says what it does and why it fits, and ends on its cost or trade-off; at most one option is marked `(recommended)` and it is listed first.

After each answer: one echo line in an exact form (`✓ N/T Label → Choice`, optionally with `(note: …)`, `(you decided: recommended)`, `(you decided: first option)` or `(from: "…")`), then the next question in the same message.

After the last answer: a bulleted list with one echo line per question, in order, then a one-sentence confirmation request; after confirmation, a short paragraph saying what will be done, then the work.

rubric.criterion: Every question uses the fallback layout: a bold `**Question N of T · Label**` heading, the question, 2-4 options as a bulleted `**X · label**: sentence` list, and one `Reply …` hint line, with no code block or box drawing.
rubric.pass: Every question has the bold heading with `N of T` and a label, the question line, 2-4 bulleted options in `**X · label**: sentence` form, and a closing `Reply …` line; nothing is fenced or boxed. (If the capture records a picker call instead, its header is at most 12 characters, the question ends with `(N of T)`, and it has 2-4 options with the recommended one first.)
rubric.partial: The layout is mostly right, but in at least one question the heading, counter, option form or reply line is missing or malformed.

rubric.criterion: Each option has one sentence saying what it does and why it fits this request, ending on its cost or trade-off.
rubric.pass: Every option on every question, the first question included, has a full sentence covering what and why that ends on a concrete cost or trade-off.
rubric.partial: Some option sentences are fragments, or skip the why or the cost/trade-off.

rubric.criterion: The rhythm holds: each answer gets a one-line echo in one of the exact forms, at the top of the message that carries the next question.
rubric.pass: Every answered question is echoed as one line in an exact form (`✓ N/T Label → Choice` with the right suffix), and that line opens the message carrying the next question or the resolved list.
rubric.partial: The rhythm mostly holds, but an echo is missing, uses a different form, or sits in a message of its own.
rubric.source: Step 4: Echo each answer, then ask the next

rubric.criterion: After the last answer the skill shows a bulleted list with one echo line per question and asks for confirmation in one sentence; once confirmed, it says what it will do in one short paragraph before doing the work.
rubric.pass: The resolved view is a bulleted list with every question's echo line in order, then a one-sentence confirmation request; after confirmation a short paragraph precedes the work.
rubric.partial: The ending is there but incomplete: a question missing from the list, the list fenced or not bulleted, a multi-sentence ask, or no paragraph before the work.

rubric.criterion: No assistant message contains more than one question.
rubric.pass: Every message asks at most one numbered question.
rubric.partial: Never applies: two questions in one message is a miss.

rubric.criterion: A question marks at most one option `(recommended)`, lists it first, and only when something the user said points to it, which its sentence names; with nothing to go on, no option is marked.
rubric.pass: Every recommendation is listed first and names something the user said; questions with nothing to go on (typically the first question on a terse request) have no recommendation.
rubric.partial: Recommendations exist, but at least one reason is generic, one is not listed first, or a question with nothing to go on is tagged anyway.

rubric.criterion: The quiz commits to its question list up front: the total T stays the same from the first question to the last and matches the questions asked, and it is no more than about seven.
rubric.pass: T never changes, equals the number of numbered questions asked, and is at most about seven (or /squiz is offered for more); any follow-up is plain prose, not a new numbered question.
rubric.partial: Within the cap, but T changes mid-quiz, doesn't match the questions asked, or a follow-up is added as a numbered question.
rubric.source: Step 1: Plan the questions before asking any

rubric.criterion: Each echo records what the user actually replied, in the matching exact form: the choice, any note, `(you decided: recommended)` or `(you decided: first option)` for a deferral, `(from: "…")` for words matched to an option.
rubric.pass: Every echo matches its reply and uses the matching form, notes and deferral markers included.
rubric.partial: One echo drops a note, uses the wrong form, or maps a free-prose or deferred reply to a debatable option.

rubric.criterion: No question, echo or resolved list is wrapped in a code block or drawn with box-drawing characters, and no emojis appear outside sample content.
rubric.pass: Questions, echoes and the resolved list are plain markdown throughout: no fences, box drawing or decorative emojis.
rubric.partial: One stray fence, box character or emoji.

rubric.criterion: The questions asked are the ones whose answers would materially change the work for this request, most load-bearing first, and none re-asks something the prompt already settled.
rubric.pass: Every question would change the resulting work, the first is the biggest decision, and nothing already stated in the prompt is asked again.
rubric.partial: Mostly right, but one question is filler, redundant with the prompt, or clearly out of order.
rubric.source: Step 1: Plan the questions before asking any; Purpose

rubric.criterion: Each card's options are realistic, distinct choices for this request, and the recommendation is the sensible default given what the user said.
rubric.pass: On every card the options are genuinely different, plausible for this request, and the recommendation fits the stated context.
rubric.partial: One card has overlapping or strawman options, or a recommendation that ignores something the user said.

rubric.criterion: The implication paragraph and the work that follows reflect every resolved answer and note, so the user gets what they chose.
rubric.pass: Every answer and note visibly shapes the implication paragraph and the delivered work; nothing chosen is dropped or contradicted.
rubric.partial: One answer or note is missing from, or softened in, the implication or the work.
rubric.appliesWhen: the run reaches confirmation and the skill begins the work
